stem:
What will be the output of the following pseudo-code?

```
Integer f(Integer n)
  if (n <= 1)
    return 1
  end if
  return n * f(n - 2)
end function

print f(7)
```
explanation: f(7) = 7 × f(5) = 7 × 5 × f(3) = 7 × 5 × 3 × f(1). f(1) hits the base case and returns 1. So f(7) = 7 × 5 × 3 × 1 = 105.
shortcut: Product of odd numbers up to 7

What will be printed by the call show(19)?

```
show(Integer n)
  if (n == 0)
    return
  end if
  show(n / 2)
  print n mod 2
end function
```

Note: / is integer division; print outputs digits without spaces.
explanation: Calls go 19 → 9 → 4 → 2 → 1 → 0. Printing happens after each recursive call returns, so remainders print from the innermost call outward: 1 mod 2 = 1, 2 mod 2 = 0, 4 mod 2 = 0, 9 mod 2 = 1, 19 mod 2 = 1, giving 10011 (binary of 19).
shortcut: Print after the recursive call = digits in correct order

Consider the function below. For which of the following calls does the recursion NEVER reach its base case?

```
Integer g(Integer n)
  if (n == 0)
    return 0
  end if
  return 1 + g(n - 2)
end function
```
explanation: Each call reduces n by 2, so n keeps its parity. Even arguments reach 0: g(6) → 4 → 2 → 0, g(4) → 2 → 0, and g(0) returns immediately. g(5) goes 5 → 3 → 1 → −1 → −3 … and skips 0, so the base case n == 0 is never met.

What will be the output of the following pseudo-code?

```
Integer calls = 0
Integer fib(Integer n)
  calls = calls + 1
  if (n < 2)
    return n
  end if
  return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
end function

Integer r = fib(5)
print r, calls
```

What will be the output of the following pseudo-code?

```
Integer h(Integer n)
  if (n > 50)
    return n - 7
  end if
  return h(h(n + 9))
end function

print h(40)
```
